name: CLTK cltk.prosody.lat scanners (hexameter, pentameter, hendecasyllable)
what: Rule-based Python scanners (Todd Cook) that syllabify a Latin line, apply position/elision rules and fit a hexameter, pentameter or Phalaecian hendecasyllable template; macrons optional.
coverage: Module files at tag v1.5.0 (commit 996acf2a6dbc, 2025-05-04): hexameter_scanner.py 488 lines, pentameter_scanner.py, hendecasyllable_scanner.py 218 lines, verse_scanner.py 465 lines, syllabifier.py, metrical_validator.py, scansion_constants.py, scansion_formatter.py, clausulae_analysis.py; CLTK 2.x (PyPI 2.5.1, master tree 182 paths) has NO prosody module.
licence_quote: MIT License Copyright (c) 2013 Classical Language Toolkit
accuracy_claim: None stated in the source files (grep for accuracy/% in the four scanner modules found nothing); file headers say __license__ = 'MIT License'.
reuse_verdict: evaluate_only: MIT code is reusable, but it is a deterministic fit-or-fail scanner without probabilities; useful as a baseline to compare against on the Hypotactic gold, and its hendecasyllable template and syllabifier rules are worth reading. Pin cltk==1.5.1 (last 1.x on PyPI) since 2.x dropped prosody.
notes: Raw sources fetched: raw.githubusercontent.com/cltk/cltk/v1.5.0/src/cltk/prosody/lat/{hexameter_scanner,pentameter_scanner,hendecasyllable_scanner,verse_scanner,scansion_constants,macronizer}.py (sha256 in fetch-log.jsonl). master tree (3a5cfb071d94) lists src/cltk/{cli,core,dependency,enrichment,genai,languages,morphosyntax,...} and no prosody.

name: CLTK macronizer + lat_models_cltk taggers/macrons (macrons.txt, macrons.py)
what: cltk.prosody.lat.macronizer (Tyler Kirby, v1.5.0) POS-tags a text (ngram/TnT/CRF taggers) and looks the (form, tag) up in vowel_len_map, a dict form -> [(tag, lemma, macronised form)] loaded from lat_models_cltk/taggers/macrons/macrons.py.
coverage: macrons.txt 29,939,283 bytes, 755,557 rows (4 tab columns: form, 9-char LDT morph tag, lemma, form with _ long / ^ short), 257,615 distinct forms; macrons.py 34,376,206 bytes (same data as a Python dict). Last commit to macrons.txt dbaf4edb2a32 2016-07-23 'Added macronizer data files'. Comparison with Winge's current macrons.txt: identical format and identical first rows ('a\te--------\ta\ta_'), 348,182 rows in common, 407,337 CLTK-only, 464,376 Winge-only (Winge has since re-run Morpheus and added ^ marks).
licence_quote: The MIT License (MIT) Copyright (c) 2014 Classical Language Toolkit
accuracy_claim: None. Docstring: 'Since the accuracy of the macronizer largely derives from the accuracy of the POS tagger used to match words to their Morpheus entry, the Macronizer class allows for multiple POS to be used.'
reuse_verdict: use (as a 2016 snapshot only): the repo says MIT, but the file is Morpheus output (Perseus, CC BY-SA 3.0 US) in Johan Winge's format, so keep the Perseus attribution and share-alike; prefer Winge's current file or regenerate from PerseusDL/morpheus stemlib. Macrons.py is the same data and not needed.
notes: Docstring (v1.5.0 macronizer.py): 'To discern whether a vowel is long, a word is first matched with its Morpheus entry by way of its POS tag. The Morpheus entry includes the macronized form of the matched word.' lat_models_cltk README is one line ('Pre-compiled taggers and tokenizers made with NLTK + CLTK data.'); no provenance statement for macrons.txt in the repo.

name: Johan Winge's Latin Macronizer (Alatius/latin-macronizer) and its macrons.txt
what: RFTagger (trained on a patched Latin Dependency Treebank, model rftagger-ldt.model 12.9 MB) picks a morph tag per token; the (form, tag) is looked up in macrons.txt, a lexicon produced by a customised Morpheus (Alatius/morpheus, Latin stemlib derived from Lewis & Short 1879) with Winge's overrides; unknown words are crunched with Morpheus at run time; scansion.py/meters.py can scan dactylic verse to disambiguate.
coverage: latin_macronizer/macrons.txt 32,929,323 bytes, 812,588 rows (form \t tag \t lemma \t accented with _ long, ^ short, _^ ambiguous), 283,023 distinct forms; vocabulary.txt 3.6 MB; macronized_endings.py 214 KB (ending->quantity by tag, generated by extractlexicon.py); lemmas.py 880 KB (LDT lemma frequencies); last commit 81f95a10a46f 2026-04-23 'Updated overrides'.
licence_quote: GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007 | README: Copyright 2015-2023 Johan Winge. You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License along with this program. If not, see <http://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
accuracy_claim: Site (alatius.com/macronizer): 'The expected accuracy on an average classical text is estimated to be about 98% to 99%.' Thesis (Winge 2015, winge2015.pdf, sha256 ae4f317a93c5): 'With RFTagger trained on either of the two corpora, the complete system was tested on four different texts and was found to agree with the human annotator on about 98% of the vowel lengths.'
reuse_verdict: ask_author: macrons.txt is a separable 33 MB data file (plain TSV, no code needed) and is the best form-level macron table available, but the repo carries only the GPL-3.0 code licence and no data statement; its content is Morpheus output (Perseus CC BY-SA 3.0 US) plus Winge's overrides. Use it now for evaluation and coverage reports; before shipping a table derived from it, ask Winge (johan.winge@gmail.com) whether the data may be redistributed under CC BY-SA 3.0/4.0 like its Morpheus source.
notes: extractlexicon.py reads macrons.txt and the LDT treebank files (treebank_data/v1.6/latin/data/*.tb.xml) to build the RFTagger lexicon, macronized_endings.py and lemmas.py. INSTALL.txt: clone Alatius/morpheus, Alatius/treebank_data, RFTagger (CIS Munich), then 'python macronize.py --initialize'. Alatius/morpheus has no LICENSE file (root: Makefile, README.md, doc, src, stemlib, tests); upstream PerseusDL/morpheus README: CC BY-SA 3.0 US (row below). Web tool at alatius.com/macronizer is the same code.

name: Collatinus lexicon with quantities (biblissima/collatinus bin/data: lemmes.la, lem_ext.la, modeles.la, irregs.la)
what: Lemma lexicon of the Collatinus lemmatiser/scanner (Yves Ouvrard, Philippe Verkerk): each lemma is written with its quantities (precomposed ā/ă etc.) plus paradigm model and radicals; modeles.la gives the endings of each paradigm with quantities, so inflected forms with quantities can be generated.
coverage: lemmes.la 1,022,434 bytes, 24,176 lines of which 104 comments = 24,072 lemma rows (Biblissima page: 24,155 lemmas, 'textes classiques du LASLA'); 22,169 rows carry macrons, 18,110 breves. lem_ext.la 2,443,437 bytes, 58,421 lines, 512 comments = 57,909 rows (site: 58,384; header: 'Extension du lexique obtenue par collation des dicos numériques', (c) Philippe Verkerk 2015); 53,841 rows with macrons. modeles.la 1,073 lines (paradigms; 'sufd:cūnquĕ' style suffix quantities); irregs.la 99 lines ('fŏrĕs:sum:164' = form with quantities:lemma:morpho ids). Format: canon_with_quantities[=graphic variant]|model|rad1|rad2|morpho note|frequency, e.g. 'lăcĭnĭa|uita|||ae, f.|7', 'Lăcō|miles|Lăcōn||onis, m.|13', 'ā=ā,ăb,ābs|inv|||prép. + abl.|5874'. Commit e1fef78818b5 2026-05-29.
licence_quote: lemmes.la header: 'COLLATINUS and PRAELECTOR are free software; you can !redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of !the GNU General Public License as published by the Free !Software Foundation; either version 2 of the License, !or (at your option) any later version.' ... '© Yves Ouvrard, 2011 - 2017'; repo LICENSE: 'GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007'; README: 'Collatinus is developed and maintained by Yves Ouvrard and Philippe Verkerk. It is made available under the [GNU GPL v3](http://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl.html) licence.'
accuracy_claim: None for quantities. Biblissima page claims ~1000 words/s lemmatisation; LASLA-frequency ranking of analyses.
reuse_verdict: use: the data files carry their own GPL-2.0-or-later header (so the licence of the data is explicit, unlike Winge's), which permits building and redistributing a derived quantity table provided that table stays under GPL-compatible terms with attribution to Ouvrard/Verkerk; keep the derived table separate from the app code. Quantities are per lemma + paradigm, not per inflected form, so a generator (modeles.la) is needed; lem_ext.la rows derived from Gaffiot 2016 were included 'avec l'autorisation de l'auteur' (Biblissima page) and are redistributed under the same GPL header.
notes: Headers in every data file say 'GNU General Public License ... either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version'; the repo LICENSE is GPL-3. Biblissima: lemmas 'extraits du Lewis & Short 1879 et du Gaffiot 2016 (avec l'autorisation de l'auteur)'; collation with Georges 1913 and Jeanneau 2017. bin/data/dicos holds only NOTES.md (38 B) in git; dictionary packages are downloaded separately from outils.biblissima.fr/collatinus/.

name: Hypotactic Latin (David Chamberlain, hypotactic.com/latin)
what: Hand syllable-by-syllable scansion of (per the Latin about page) 'pretty much all of non-fragmentary Early, Classical and Silver Latin verse' as static HTML: one div per poem, one div per line, span per word, span per syllable with class long/short/elided plus modifiers.
coverage: Per-work files https://hypotactic.com/latin/<id>.html, ids from authors.html (menu: li onclick="loadup('<id>', this)"). Catullus: catullus.html 1,449,611 bytes, 3,037 lines, sha256 ff1ac5d6cc9eb963027acf440acaaa5aecc0d6bda25c44a5e1d063a8142814b8: 118 poem divs (1-116 with 2b, 14b, 58b; 18-20 absent as in modern editions), 2,301 line divs, 29,528 syllable spans (long 17,406, short 10,906, elided 1,137, hiatus 55, elided hypermetric 9, resolved 8, systole 1, synizesis 1, semihiatus 1, halffoot 1, lengthening 1, diastole 1); poems by data-metre: elegy 54, hendecasyllables 43, scazon 8, sapadon 2, ia6 2, glycpher 2, hexameter 2, ia6g 1, priapean 1, iamtetcata 1, asc5 1, galliamb 1. Horace: odes1.html 464,420 bytes, 1,397 lines, sha256 3ea6ee35b5335f30bd6c22c07d94aa17e49a422a84f8d27ae173fef672b76901: 38 poems, 876 lines, 9,387 syllables (long 5,674, short 3,593, elided 110, lengthening 5, hiatus 4, synezesis 1); metres alcaic 10, sapadon 9, asc2 4, asc3 4, asc4 4, alcmanic_strophe 2, asc5 2, asc1 1, arch4 1, sapphic2 1; line-level classes 'line asc1', 'line glyconic', 'line iambic', 'line d4_tr3'. Horace menu: Odes 1-4 (odes1..odes4), Epodes (epodes), Sermones, Epistulae, Ars Poetica (arspoetica); Carmen Saeculare is NOT in the menu (string 'saecul' absent from authors.html; odes4 not fetched). Whole-site Latin data zip: https://hypotactic.com/hypotactic_data_6_17_2025.zip, 29,084,693 bytes, Last-Modified 17 Jun 2025 (HEAD only).
licence_quote: All the data on this site is/are licensed as CC-BY 4.0 . That means that you can use it as you wish, but if you make significant or extensive use of it in published work you should reference me (David Chamberlain) and this site (hypotactic.com) as the source of the information (this constitutes my interpretation of the licence's "reasonable manner" language). By "data" I mean the tagging of individual syllables of verse with metrical attributes such as quantity, elision, hiatus, synizesis etc., and the identification of those syllables as independent metrical units.* To be clear, I do not intend to place any restrictions that go beyond standard academic attribution conventions; rather, I would like to encourage others to use the data as they will. The licence is intended to reassure you that that's OK.
accuracy_claim: Hand scansion; no error rate stated. The Greek-side README of Urdatorn/hypotactic calls it the author's own tagging; corrections ongoing per the about page.
reuse_verdict: use (gold only, never in the lexicon): CC BY 4.0 stated on the Latin about page itself, so the Greek survey's wish for a Latin-side statement is met. Attribute 'David Chamberlain, hypotactic.com'.
notes:
Span format:
...
Cuidōnō...; Horace poems add data-book="1"; elision = class 'syll elided' (text keeps the letters, e.g. 'ce' in 'pūmice expolītum'); synizesis = 'syll long synizesis' (Odes file spells it 'synezesis'); hiatus = 'syll long hiatus'/'syll short hiatus'; lengthening/diastole/systole/semihiatus/halffoot/resolved res1,res2/hypermetric as extra classes; stanza divs; macrons written in the text (option 'Macrons'). metredivs.html lists template ids ia6, senarii, ia6g, ia7, ia8, tr7, hendecasyllables, scazon, cr4, hexameter, elegy. The site's data page: 'A very preliminary version of the Latin data is now available ... https://hypotactic.com/hypotactic_data_6_17_2025.zip'. Raw pages: raw/hypotactic-latin-{index,about,authors,metredivs,catullus-probe,odes1}.html, raw/hypotactic-metre.js.

name: Pedecerto (pedecerto.eu) / Musisque Deoque (mqdq.it) automatic scansions
what: Pedecerto's machine scansion (with manual checking) of the MQDQ corpus, searchable on the web and downloadable as XML per author ('Scarica come XML', form POST /pagine/autori) or as one zip of everything ('Scarica tutte le scansioni' -> /allpedecertoscans.zip).
coverage: allpedecertoscans.zip: 12,019,593 bytes, Last-Modified 18 Aug 2025 (HEAD only, not downloaded). Author list includes Catullus (letter C) and Horatius (letter H). XML schema on the page: line attributes name, meter (symbol H, P, A, Y, N, S, L, D, C, F, O, I, G, T, R, V; 'solo H e P sono analizzati' = only hexameter and pentameter lines are scanned), pattern (first four feet D/S, fifth only if spondaic), features (spondaic, hypermeter); word attributes sy (syllables: A arsis, T thesis of spondee, b/c thesis of dactyl), wb (CM masculine caesura, CF feminine, DI diaeresis), mf (SY synaloephe, HI hiatus, PH prosodic hiatus, DS final s dropped, PE prodelision). So for Catullus only the elegiacs/hexameters (62, 64, 65-116) and for Horace only Sermones/Epistulae/Ars are scanned; no hendecasyllables, no Odes.
licence_quote: pedecerto.eu footer: '© 2007 - Musisque Deoque © 2011 - Pede certo Tutti i diritti riservati' ... 'Non ne è consentito alcun uso a scopi commerciali se non previo accordo. Sono consentite la riproduzione e la circolazione in formato cartaceo o su supporto elettronico portatile (off-line) ad esclusivo uso scientifico, didattico o documentario, purché i documenti non vengano alterati in alcun modo sostanziale, ed in particolare mantengano le corrette indicazioni di data, paternità e fonte originale (citazione). Link da altri siti web sono graditi, soprattutto se ne verrà data comunicazione alla redazione ( mqdq-galaxy@unive.it ), per facilitare la tempestiva comunicazione di eventuali successive variazioni. È vietato ogni genere di mirroring (duplicazione) su altri siti, o di cattura automatica dei testi, a meno di specifici accordi con la redazione.' | mqdq.it: 'Tutti i diritti dei testi con apparato contenuti in www.mqdq.it sono riservati alle unità del Progetto Ricerca di Interesse Nazionale Musisque Deoque , ai curatori editoriali dell'opera e agli autori originari dei documenti. Non ne è consentito alcun uso a scopi commerciali se non previo accordo.'
accuracy_claim: None on the site pages fetched; Nolden 2022 (Leiden thesis) and anceps use Pedecerto scansions as training/ground truth.
reuse_verdict: ask_author: the terms allow reproduction 'in formato cartaceo o su supporto elettronico portatile (off-line) ad esclusivo uso scientifico, didattico o documentario' without alteration and with source citation, forbid commercial use without agreement and forbid mirroring or automatic capture without agreement. An offline evaluation run against the site's own zip fits 'uso scientifico' but greeklyric.com is a product, so write to mqdq-galaxy@unive.it before use; even then the data only covers dactylic lines, which the Catullus hendecasyllable target does not need.
notes: No scraping done: index, /pagine/autori (+ ?lettera=C, ?lettera=H), /pagine/arte and progettometastasio presentation page fetched; /cookies.php returned 500. mqdq.it links to MQDQ Galaxy (pric.unive.it/projects/mqdq-galaxy). Raw: raw/pedecerto-*.html, raw/mqdq-*.html.

name: Anceps (dargones/anceps, Sasha Fedchin)
what: Constraint-based scanner: enumerates all macronisations of a line consistent with the metre (trimeter focus), using Winge's Morpheus dictionary plus frequency dictionaries built from Pedecerto/MQDQ scansions; CLI for manual resolution of the ~10% of trimeters it cannot decide.
coverage: data/: MorpheusMacrons.txt 32,929,381 bytes (same size class as Winge's macrons.txt), MqDqMacrons.json 18,916,572 bytes, MqDqMacronsNoDiphthongs.json 18,843,331, PoetiDItaliaMacrons.json 37,954,776, fullScansions/Agamemnon.json, manualScansions/Agamemnon.txt (552 B), texts/Agamemnon.txt; last push 2022-02-07; 14 stars.
accuracy_claim: README: 'A substantial portion of the lines (around 10%) must be scanned manually' (trimeter); no accuracy figure.
reuse_verdict: ask_author: no LICENSE file in the repo (GitHub licence field null) and the MQDQ-derived frequency dictionaries inherit the MQDQ terms; the method (metre as constraint over a quantity lexicon) is the one Melos already uses, so there is little to take beyond the idea.
notes: README fetched (raw/anceps-README.md); data listing via GitHub API (raw/ghapi-repos_dargones_anceps_contents_data_ref_master.json). Not the Ben Nagy tool the brief guessed at; no 'anceps' by Nagy found.

name: Gaffiot 2016 (Gérard Gréco et al.; gaffiot.fr, gaffiot.org)
what: Digitised Félix Gaffiot Latin-French dictionary with quantities on headwords (gaffiot.org list: 'ăbăcīnus', 'ăbāctĭō' ...); gaffiot.fr serves it as a 21.6 MB JS object.
coverage: gaffiot.fr/gaffiot.js 21,616,171 bytes (fetched inadvertently as a 'script'; header '/* gaffiot.fr - Tous droits réservés */'); Gréco's database zip described as 5.5 MB.
licence_quote: Nous mettons à disposition cette ressource électronique structurée, protégée par le code de la propriété intellectuelle sur les bases de données (L341-1), selon les termes de la licence Creative Commons : « Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International ». Les organisations Wikipedia, Wiktionary, Wikisources et similaires sont exclues du bénéfice de cette licence. Toute autorisation au-delà du champ de cette licence doit être obtenue auprès de nous. (Wayback Machine copy of Gréco's page, fetched 2026-10-11) | gaffiot.fr: 'gaffiot.fr - Tous droits réservés'; gaffiot.fr about: 'Le contenu du Gaffiot 2016 est corrigé et publié avec l'autorisation de M. Gréco'
reuse_verdict: no: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 forbids derived tables (ND) and commercial use, and the Wiktionary exclusion shows the author's intent; Collatinus's lem_ext.la already carries the Gaffiot lemmas under GPL by the author's permission, which is the only route.
notes: Licence quoted from a web.archive.org snapshot because gerardgreco.free.fr is the original; gaffiot.org's front page states no licence.

name: Whitaker's Words (mk270/whitakers-words)
what: Latin-English dictionary with inflectional morphology (Ada); the lexicon has no vowel-length marks.
coverage: Repo pushed 2026-08-26; README: 'it does not currently support vowel length'.
licence_quote: Permission is hereby freely given for any and all use of program and data. You can sell it as your own, but at least tell me. ... All parts of the WORDS system, source code and data files, are made freely available to anyone who wishes to use them, for whatever purpose.
reuse_verdict: no (for quantities): no macrons at all; could serve as a permissively licensed lemmatiser fallback.
notes: LICENSE file 404 at master; the licence text lives in README 'Licensing' (GitHub API: NOASSERTION).

name: Logeion (logeion.uchicago.edu)
what: Aggregated Latin/Greek lexica with a private API; off limits per the Greek survey.
coverage: Home page 1,870 bytes, JS app; no terms text.
reuse_verdict: no: no licence or terms published; not used.
notes: Noted only, as instructed.

name: KaanGoker/dactylic-hexameter-latin-poetry-corpus (HF)
what: Plain-text corpus (~56,000 hexameter lines of Vergil, Ovid, Statius, Lucan, Silius, Juvenal from The Latin Library) for LLM fine-tuning; no scansion marks.
coverage: latin_hexameter_corpus.txt; size category 10K<n<100K; last modified 2026-01-03.
reuse_verdict: no: text only, from The Latin Library (its own terms unverified); no quantities.
notes: HF dataset search for 'macron', 'macronized', 'latin scansion', 'vowel length' found no Latin macron dataset; only Greek (Macronizer/norma, Ericu950/oga-macronized).

name: Macronised Latin text corpora on GitHub (austintheriot/nova-vulgata-with-macrons; DoctrinaLatina/doctrina-latina; njand/lat_text_latin_library_macronized; increpare/metamorphosespdf)
what: Hand- or machine-macronised running texts (Nova Vulgata by hand; Latin Library and Metamorphoses auto-macronised with Winge's tool).
coverage: GitHub API licence field: null / NOASSERTION for all four.
reuse_verdict: no: no licence, and the auto-macronised ones add nothing beyond Winge's lexicon; hand-macronised Nova Vulgata could be an evaluation text if its author grants a licence (ask).
